---
title: Vivacious Cloud
description: How to launch Axolotl with preflight VRAM estimation and multi-cloud GPU provisioning on Vivacious Cloud
---

[Vivacious Cloud](https://vivaciouscloud.com) is a unified multi-cloud GPU orchestrator and preflight validation platform designed to prevent Out-Of-Memory (CUDA OOM) failures and simplify distributed training. It allows developers to run Axolotl jobs across heterogeneous cloud providers (including AWS, RunPod, Lambda Labs, and GCP) with automatic preflight memory verification.

You can also use the open-source companion CLI [`vivacious-cli`](https://github.com/Viavcious-cloud/vivacious-cli) to calculate exact model weight, optimizer state, and activation memory requirements locally before spinning up cloud instances.

## Preflight Memory Check

Before launching training runs, verify that your model, sequence length, and batch configuration will fit within your target GPU VRAM:

```bash
pip install vivacious-cli
```

Estimate memory requirements for your Axolotl training configuration:

```bash
vivacious estimate \
  --model meta-llama/Llama-3.2-3B \
  --seq-len 4096 \
  --batch-size 4 \
  --method lora \
  --rank 16
```

The CLI outputs an allocation audit:
- **Base Model Parameters**: Raw bfloat16 weight allocation
- **Optimizer States**: AdamW / 8-bit AdamW memory footprint
- **Activation Memory**: Attention context expansion with sequence packing
- **Headroom Margin**: Safety buffer required to avoid allocator thrashing

## Launching Axolotl with Vivacious Cloud

### 1. Provision GPU Compute

Select your optimal hardware through Vivacious Cloud or via CLI:

```bash
# Provision a spot or on-demand RTX 4090 or A100 across 12+ cloud providers
vivacious provision --gpu rtx4090 --provider auto
```

### 2. Run Axolotl Fine-Tuning

Inside your instance, clone your repository or use the pre-configured Axolotl environment:

```bash
git clone https://github.com/axolotl-ai-cloud/axolotl.git
cd axolotl
pip install -e .
```

Launch training with your YAML config:

```bash
accelerate launch -m axolotl.cli.train examples/llama-3/lora-3b.yml
```

### 3. Failover & Checkpoint Resilience

Vivacious Cloud monitors spot instance health. If an upstream cloud provider signals instance reclamation, warm checkpoints saved to your configured S3/GCS bucket ensure seamless resumption without loss of training progress.
